newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon up on T$400 bln project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon up on T$400 bln project.

text.p: Leading microchip maker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co surged at mid-morning on Friday after announcing a T$400 billion, 10-year wafer fab project on Thursday, brokers said.
With 75 minutes left, Taiwan Semiconductor rose the daily seven percent limit to T$85.

Taiwan Semiconductor said it would pour T$400 billion into southern Taiwan's Tainan Science-based Industrial Park over the next 10 years to build six world-class wafer fabrication plants, including eight-inch and 12-inch fabs.
The investment would be Taiwan's largest single industrial project -- bigger even than Formosa group's huge T$240 billion refinery and petrochemical complex at southern Yunlin.
Analysts said the investment was necessary for Taiwan's top chipmaker to stay ahead amid fierce international competition and would ensure the firm's leading position in Taiwan.

"Taiwan Semiconductor's foundry business is expected to continue high growth in coming years and its big investment project will ensure its leading position among Taiwan's chipmakers," said Michael Hung, an independent analyst.
Taiwan Semicondutor reported 1996 earnings per share of T$7.3 and expected to make T$3.7 for 1997.
"Taiwan Semiconductor should be able to make an EPS of around T$4 in 1997 and more than T$5 in 1998," Hung said.
"Its share price likely will double in the next 12 months," he said.
